batchName: Middle Republic: Scipio and the Road to Zama (216-201 BCE) - Medium Batch 1
chapterName: Middle Republic: Scipio and the Road to Zama (216-201 BCE)

questions.question: What scene, a favourite of Renaissance painters, is known as the "Continence of Scipio"?
options: Scipio freeing Spanish hostages without conditions
Scipio refusing to become consul for life and dictator
Scipio rejecting Hannibal's terms before Zama
Scipio returning a beautiful captive untouched to her fiancé
Scipio sparing the citizens of Gades after its surrender
questions.explanation: In this tale from a much later writer, Scipio gave a beautiful captive back unharmed to her Spanish fiancé. Scipio also treated the 300 Spanish hostages in New Carthage generously.
questions.sourceQuote: In it, Scipio returned a beautiful captive untouched to her Spanish fiancé.

questions.question: According to one ancient account, what did young Scipio do in the cavalry clash on the river Ticinus?
options: Carried news of the defeat to Rome
Led the charge that won the battle
Saved his surrounded father's life
Captured several of Hannibal's elephants
Killed a Carthaginian general in single combat
questions.explanation: One account says Scipio rescued his father when enemy horsemen surrounded him. Other writers gave the credit to an unnamed slave.
questions.sourceQuote: According to one ancient account, enemy horsemen surrounded Scipio's father in a cavalry clash on the river Ticinus in northern Italy, and young Scipio saved his life.

questions.question: How do historians regard the famous story of Hannibal ranking the greatest generals in conversation with Scipio?
options: They date it to the parley before Zama
They accept it because Polybius reports it
They consider the meeting apocryphal
They trace it to Scipio's lost memoirs
They think the speaker was Masinissa
questions.explanation: Historians think this meeting never happened. It belongs with the many legends that grew around Scipio.
questions.sourceQuote: A famous story has Hannibal later ranking the greatest generals in conversation with Scipio, but historians consider the meeting apocryphal.

questions.question: Who made up the core of the army Scipio took to Africa?
options: Veterans of the victory at the Metaurus
Numidian horsemen sent by Masinissa
Fresh conscripts called up in Rome
Spanish tribesmen recruited after Ilipa
Two legions of Cannae survivors posted to Sicily
questions.explanation: Scipio's core force was two legions of men who had survived Cannae and been sent to Sicily. He drilled the army for about a year.
questions.sourceQuote: The core of his force was two legions (*legiones*) made up of survivors of Cannae who had been posted to Sicily.

questions.question: What war indemnity did Carthage have to pay under the peace of 201 BC?
options: 40 tonnes of gold paid at once
1,000 silver talents over 10 years
10,000 silver talents over 50 years
3,200 silver talents over 50 years
5,000 silver talents over 20 years
questions.explanation: Carthage had to pay 10,000 silver talents over half a century. It also gave up its war elephants.
questions.sourceQuote: It had to pay 10,000 silver talents over 50 years, gave up its war elephants and kept only ten warships.

questions.question: What do modern scholars suspect really lay behind Scipio's appointment to Spain?
options: The army in Spain proclaimed him its general
His uncle had named him successor before dying
The consuls drew lots and his name came up
The people forced him on a strongly unwilling Senate
Senators chose him, then had the people vote to make it look legitimate
questions.explanation: Scholars think the Senate picked Scipio and used a popular vote to legitimise an irregular command. A Roman historian two centuries later instead portrayed the Senate as dithering.
questions.sourceQuote: Modern scholars suspect instead that the senators picked Scipio themselves, then had the people vote on it to make an irregular command look legitimate.

questions.question: How did Scipio arrange his infantry maniples at Zama to deal with Hannibal's elephants?
options: Behind a line of sharpened stakes and trenches
Packed tightly into a single solid square
In their usual staggered, chessboard-like pattern
One behind another, leaving open lanes filled with skirmishers
Spread thinly along a ridge above the plain
questions.explanation: Instead of the normal staggered formation, Scipio lined up his maniples to create lanes. Most of the elephants ran down these lanes, where they were cut off and killed.
questions.sourceQuote: Instead he lined them up one behind another, leaving open lanes filled with light skirmishers (*velites*).

questions.question: Why might Polybius's picture of Scipio be flattering, despite his general reliability?
options: He was close to Scipio's family, and his main informant was Scipio's friend
He had served as an officer in Scipio's African army
He was paid by the Senate to glorify Roman generals
He relied only on Scipio's own Greek memoirs
He was Scipio's son and wrote a family history
questions.explanation: Polybius was a close friend of Scipio's relatives, and his main informant was Scipio's second-in-command. Scipio's own memoirs and his son's history are lost.
questions.sourceQuote: But he was a close friend of Scipio's relatives, and his main informant about Scipio was Scipio's own friend and second-in-command, so his picture may be flattering.

questions.question: What made Scipio's command in Spain unprecedented?
options: He was the first Roman to command an army overseas
He was appointed directly by a dictator
He got consular power without ever having been consul
He was chosen by the Senate alone, without a vote
He shared command with a Numidian prince
questions.explanation: Scipio had held none of Rome's senior offices, yet he received the full military authority of a consul. No Roman had been given such power before without first serving as consul.
questions.sourceQuote: He was the first Roman ever given such power without first serving as consul.

questions.question: What weakness in New Carthage's defences did Scipio exploit?
options: Its walls had been damaged by an earthquake
The harbour was left unguarded during a festival
The lagoon on its north side could be waded at low tide
A traitor opened the main gate at night
The citadel had run out of drinking water
questions.explanation: Scipio sent a party across the shallow lagoon while the walls were under attack. He told his troops Neptune had promised him help.
questions.sourceQuote: A lagoon guarded the city's northern side, but at low tide it could be waded.
